provisions.title: Collection and sharing of consumer health data by regulated entity prohibited; exceptions
provisions.quote: With the affirmative, voluntary consent of the consumer to whom the consumer health data relates, which must be separate and distinct from the consent provided pursuant to subsection 1 for the collection of the data;
provisions.appliesTo: "Regulated entity" means any person who: 1. Conducts business in this State or produces or provides products or services that are targeted to consumers in this State; and 2. Alone or with other persons, determines the purpose and means of processing, sharing or selling consumer health data. (NRS 603A.465)

provisions.title: Unauthorized sale or offering of consumer health data prohibited; required contents of authorization
provisions.quote: A person who sells consumer health data shall provide a copy of the written authorization provided pursuant to subsection 1 to the consumer who signed the written authorization and the purchaser of the consumer health data.
provisions.appliesTo: Any person who sells or offers to sell consumer health data. The written authorization must include the signature of the consumer to which the consumer health data pertains.

provisions.title: SB 370 effective date

consumer_health_data.note: SB 370 (NRS 603A.400 to 603A.550) applies to any regulated entity. It requires consent to collect or share and a signed written authorization to sell. In force since 31 March 2024.

crossCheck.note: Quotes match NRS 603A.500 and 603A.535. Separate consent to share is in 603A.500(2). Ch. 525 (SB 370) sec. 36 sets 31 March 2024. Regulated entity in 603A.465 is general in scope.

freeCopyCases: Records needed to support a claim or appeal under the Social Security Act or a federal or state financial needs-based benefit program, for the patient or an authorized representative, with documentation of the claim (NRS 629.061(5)). First copy free; a second copy for the same claim may cost up to 60 cents per page.
feeRules: NRS 629.061(4): copy for actual postage and copying cost, "not to exceed 60 cents per page for photocopies"; "No administrative fee or additional service fee of any kind may be charged for furnishing such a copy."
NRS 629.062(2): electronic copy fee "must not exceed $40 or the amount per page prescribed by NRS 629.061, whichever is less."
NRS 629.062(3)-(4): a $5 minimum fee, and $5, $20 and $25 fees for no-records confirmation, custodian certificate, film sheets and radiologic images (not for state or local government custodians).

provisions.title: Health care records: inspection; copies and related charges
provisions.quote: or under any federal or state financial needs-based benefit program, without charge, to a patient, or a representative with written authorization from the patient, who requests it, if the request is accompanied by documentation of the claim or appeal.
provisions.appliesTo: Each custodian of health care records. The free copy is due within 30 days after receipt of the request.

provisions.title: Health care records: copy fee cap
provisions.quote: the costs of making the copy, not to exceed 60 cents per page for photocopies and a reasonable cost for copies of X-ray photographs and other health care records produced by similar processes.
provisions.appliesTo: Each custodian of health care records. Records must be available for inspection within 10 working days (in state); no deadline is set for copies.

provisions.title: Furnishing of records electronically: request; method; fees
provisions.quote: any fee to furnish those records electronically pursuant to subsection 1 must not exceed $40 or the amount per page prescribed by NRS 629.061, whichever is less.
provisions.appliesTo: Custodians of health care records, including HIPAA covered entities and business associates. SB 283 sets no effective date, so NRS 218D.330 default of October 1 applies.

copy_rights.note: Free copy for Social Security and needs-based benefit claims goes beyond HIPAA and Part 171. No copy deadline under 30 days; the 10 working day rule covers inspection only. Fee caps are recorded as facts.

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor yes: a free copy for a benefits claim goes past HIPAA and Part 171. No copy deadline under 30 days. Current 629.061 text from AB 474 (2017), effective 1 Jan 2018. SB 283 sec. 8 sets 1 Oct 2023.

provisions.title: Communicable disease information: confidentiality; permissible disclosure
provisions.citation: NRS 441A.220 (as amended by 2025 Nev. Stat. ch. 514, SB 494, sec. 205)
provisions.quote: is confidential medical information and must not be disclosed to any person under any circumstances, including pursuant to any subpoena, search warrant or discovery proceeding, except:
provisions.appliesTo: Personal information about a person who has a communicable disease. Subsection 9 names persons diagnosed with the human immunodeficiency virus.

hiv.note: The rule covers all communicable diseases, and an exception in subsection 9 names HIV. Disclosure is limited to listed cases, including written consent.

crossCheck.note: Rule covers communicable disease information; subsection 9 names HIV. SB 494 (2025) sec. 205 amends it; sec. 372 sets 1 July 2025.

provisions.title: Disclosure of identity or genetic information of person without consent unlawful; exceptions
provisions.citation: NRS 629.171 (as amended by 2023 Nev. Stat. ch. 386, SB 283)
provisions.quote: It is unlawful to disclose or to compel a person to disclose the identity of a person who was the subject of a genetic test or to disclose genetic information of that person in a manner that allows identification of the person, without first obtaining the informed consent

genetic.note: NRS 629.171 requires informed consent before identifying genetic information is disclosed, with listed exceptions.

prohibitions: NRS 629.610(1): "a provider of mental and behavioral health care shall not use an artificial intelligence system in connection with providing professional mental and behavioral health care directly to a patient."

NRS 433.567(2): "An artificial intelligence provider shall not make available for use by a person in this State an artificial intelligence system that is specifically programmed to provide a service or experience to a user that would constitute the practice of professional mental or behavioral health care if provided by a natural person."

provisions.title: Certain uses of artificial intelligence systems prohibited; exceptions for administrative support tasks
provisions.quote: A provider of mental and behavioral health care shall independently review the accuracy of any report, data or other information compiled, summarized, analyzed or generated by an artificial intelligence system for a purpose described in paragraph (c) or (e) of subsection 2.
provisions.appliesTo: Licensed or certified providers of mental and behavioral health care (psychiatrists, psychologists, clinical social workers, psychiatric nurses, therapists, counselors).

provisions.title: Prohibited activity of artificial intelligence provider
provisions.quote: An artificial intelligence provider shall not make available for use by a person in this State an artificial intelligence system that is specifically programmed to provide a service or experience to a user that would constitute the practice of professional mental or behavioral health care
provisions.appliesTo: Artificial intelligence providers offering systems to persons in Nevada.
